requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation of `requirements.references.coverage.report` has an {impl} item that carries it out and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**

1. **`habeas status` warns about every item without recent coverage, naming file, line, kind, and name.**
   - `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` collects `UncoveredItem`s. Its `uncovered_error` message names the file, line, kind, and name, followed by "has no recent coverage".
   - `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` drops items that `RecentCoverage::covers` finds in the current or last-N versions of the evidence files. `RecentCoverage::covers` is reached from `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` through `RecentCoverage::load` and `RecentCoverage::add_history`.
   - `src/commands.rs#fn[inspected_coverage_warnings]` and `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_section]` render these as the "Coverage warnings" section.
   - Test: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts the section and the warning line for `render`.
   - Test: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` asserts the window behaviour. `helper` is warned about at once, and `parse` is warned about only after the third re-authoring.

2. **`habeas author` warns after it finishes.**
   - `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` writes the warnings to stderr. `src/main.rs#fn[main]` calls it after a batch (unless cancelled), after a kept-current single subject, and after a single authored subject, including with `--stdout`.
   - Tests: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]`. Both assert the per-item line on stderr. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics]` assert the incomplete-history note.

3. **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
   - `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_module]` handles inline `mod tests`, and `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_file]` handles out-of-line `tests.rs` and `tests/` modules. Both set `in_tests`, which `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` filters on.
   - Tests: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` (a `fixture` in an inline `mod tests` is not warned about), `tests/coverage.rs#fn[items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about]`, and `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]`.

4. **A warning MUST NOT fail validation.**
   - The warnings live in the separate `uncovered` list. Only untested `#[test]` functions are pushed to `errors`, in `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]`.
   - Test: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` asserts that validation reports no error for `parse`. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` asserts validation has no errors.

5. **Repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.**
   - A search of `src` finds `git2` used only in `src/coverage_history.rs`, reached only from `coverage_history::warnings`. `inspect_repository` does not call it.
   - Test: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` deletes the Git object store and asserts validation output is unchanged.

**Other checks**
- Behaviour beyond the text, such as the incomplete-history note, is specified by `requirements.references.coverage.history`, which the same code marks {impl}.
- I found no unspecified behaviour in the {impl} code.
- I found no {fixme} references.

text: :::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
